newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan THK says to start shipments from China plant.
newsitem.headline: Japan THK says to start shipments from China plant.

text.p: Japan's THK Co Ltd said on Tuesday it would start shipments of linear motion guide systems from its China plant as early as this month.
The systems are used in semiconductor manufacturing machines and other industrial machines.

THK president Akihiro Teramachi said in an interview that the company's China plant was set up as a joint venture and that 80 to 90 percent of the products made there would be shipped to other Asian countries.
Teramachi said the output level at the Chinese plant will be formally announced later this month.
THK has a 60 percent share of the global market for the systems, although its market share in Asia was lower, at levels of about 40 percent to 50 percent.

He also said his company expects to receive orders worth more than 51 billion yen in the first half of this business year, up two billion yen from its earlier estimate. This could lead to an upward revision in the company's profit estimates, he said.
In June, THK predicted that its group net profit would be around nine billion yen for the year to March 1998, three times its actual year-earlier profit of 3.02 billion.

The company also announced in late June that it will build its first plant in the United States to produce the linear motion guide systems. It said it would form a firm in Ohio in July to build a factory to start operations next year.
